newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Giant zinc mine in doubt as Aborigine talks fail.
newsitem.headline: Giant zinc mine in doubt as Aborigine talks fail.

text.p: The future of Australia's A$1.0 billion (US$760 million) Century zinc mine, potentially the world's largest, was under threat on Friday after negotiations between mine owner RTZ-CRA and Aborigines collapsed.
Asked if the outback Queensland mine would go ahead, state premier Rob Borbidge said: "I wouldn't hold my breath".
"We obviously are disappointed that the negotiations did not produce a result," a spokesman for RTZ-CRA subsidiary Century Zinc Ltd told Reuters.

The company had expected to forge an agreement with Aboriginal groups by midnight (1300 GMT) Thursday, but withdrew a A$60 million jobs and compensation package when only four of the 12 groups claiming a right to the land would sign the agreement.
A landmark court ruling in 1992 determined that Aborigines might still have rights to their traditional lands.

This creates a clash between Aborigines and primary producers who want to use the land and the legislative framework set up to regulate native title gives Aborigines a right to negotiate over development.
If an agreement on Century is not reached in the next few days the issue will move to the Native Title Tribunal, which can take up to six months to forge a binding agreement.
Borbidge said the collapse of the deal highlighted the inadequacies of the native title process.

Another court decision in December widened the clash between Aborigines' native title and primary producers by ruling -- contrary to previous assumptions -- that Aborigines still had rights even when a pastoral lease had been granted over the land.
Prime Minister John Howard on Friday met groups arguing for and against parliament neutralising the latest ruling.

Farmers and others generally want parliament to simply abolish native title in land covered by a lease but others, noting that much of the worry is caused by uncertainty, want just a definition of what Aborigines are entitled to.
RTZ-CRA has said disintegration of the Century talks could also jeopardise plans to sell the mine to metals miner Pasminco as the sale depended on the signing of a native title deal.
However, Pasminco denied on Friday that the breakdown of the talks would threaten the deal, saying it had allowed for a period of arbitration.
Pasminco has made a downpayment of A$10 million on the mine with the remainder of the A$345 million sale price payable only if valid leases are granted.
